export_evidence: ImportKey page for slug 'cosmos-surgical-equipments-private-limited' shows 148 records, but every visible row is an INBOUND shipment into India, e.g. "2025-12-05 | Tonglu WANHE Medical Instrument Co.,Ltd. -> COSMOS SURGICAL EQUIPMENTS PRIVATE LIMITED | HF2006.3A Scissor | HANGCHOW HANGZHOU, CHINA -> CHENNAI AIR CARGO ACC, India | HS 90189099 | BOL 6120039". No outbound (India -> foreign destination) bill of lading with date, destination and HS code was found on any accessible source.
domestic_evidence: No GST turnover band, GeM/CPPP tender award, contract or annual-report split could be retrieved: web_search returned 'no results (searx: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>)' for the query on GST turnover/GeM tenders, and thecompanycheck.com returned 'fetch_error: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden'. Domestic supply therefore not verified either way.
note: Source counter vs rows seen: ImportKey header states 'Total Shipments 148 Records detected' and 'Trading Partners 2 Known counterparties', but only 5 shipment rows were rendered in the free view (latest 2025-12-05, oldest shown 2025-04-10); all 5 are imports into India, HS 90189099 / 85285900, ports Chennai Air Cargo ACC, Hangzhou, Amsterdam Schiphol, Seoul Incheon. Two other slug variants ('cosmos-surgical-equipments-pvt-ltd', 'cosmos-surgical-equipments') returned empty record tables. volza.com and eximpedia.app both returned HTTP 403, so no second source could be cross-checked. IMPORTANT: the declared HS 901811 (electro-cardiographs) does not match the observed trade HS 90189099 (other surgical/medical instruments) — per project rules this is not a rejection ground; the company is a surgical-instrument importer/distributor, not a manufacturer with proven export flows. No export shipments and no domestic supply evidence found; the only factual activity is inbound purchasing from Chinese and Dutch suppliers. Revenue and export volume: null (not public in accessible sources). Note also that the claimed industry 'Нефтегаз и химия' (oil & gas / chemicals) contradicts the observed medical-device trade data.
